questions.q: What is the AWS root user?
options: A temporary identity that expires after 90 days
A read-only identity used only for billing reports
An IAM user created by an administrator for daily tasks
The identity created automatically with the AWS account, tied to the sign-up email, with unrestricted access to everything in the account
questions.explain: Root is created the moment the account is signed up for, identified by the sign-up email rather than a username, and has complete access to the account.

questions.q: Why is root risky to use for everyday administration?
options: It is slower to use than an IAM user
It automatically deletes resources after each login
It has no permission boundary — it can affect every service, resource, and billing detail in the account with no restrictions possible
It cannot access the AWS Management Console at all
questions.explain: Unlike IAM identities, root can't be restricted by a permissions policy — it can do anything the account is capable of.

questions.q: What is the first step in the real best-practice sequence for securing root?
options: Share the root password with the whole team
Disable billing access for root
Delete the root user immediately
Enable MFA (multi-factor authentication) on the root user
questions.explain: MFA is enabled on root first, so a leaked password alone isn't enough for someone to sign in as root.

questions.q: After securing root, what should be created for daily administrative work?
options: An IAM user with administrator permissions, used for everyday sign-in instead of root
A second root account with the same email
A public access key shared across the team
Nothing — root should still be used daily
questions.explain: An IAM administrator user (e.g., with the AdministratorAccess policy) replaces root for day-to-day work, and root is locked away.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a task that genuinely still requires signing in as root?
options: Launching an EC2 instance
Closing the AWS account entirely
Writing an IAM policy for a new group
Creating an S3 bucket
questions.explain: Closing the account, changing root's own email/password, and certain billing tasks are among the few actions that can't be delegated away from root.
